sections.heading: What is checked before an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Seawoods reaches your door
paragraphs: Before a profile is shown to you, the tutor's identity document and highest qualification are checked, and their claimed board experience is tested rather than taken on trust. The useful question is not whether they have taught the IB; it is which components. A tutor who says they teach Diploma Programme Biology is asked which internal assessment criteria they have marked work against and what they do with a student whose investigation has no valid independent variable. Vague answers end the conversation. Someone in Seawoods searching for an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Seawoods deserves to know that the filter ran before the shortlist, not after a wasted month.

You should still run your own checks, because you can see things a platform cannot. Ask the tutor to mark one of your child's returned answers in front of you and explain the marks lost. Ask what grade boundaries did last session in that subject and whether they moved. Ask which textbook or past-paper series they will use and why. Ask them to say, out loud, what they expect to be different in four weeks. A tutor who can answer those four questions has planned the term. A tutor who answers all four with reassurance has planned the first session.

Then the practical layer, which in a gated Seawoods complex is where good arrangements fail. Register the tutor with your society office as a regular visitor in the first week rather than signing them in as a guest every Tuesday, because the fourth time a tutor waits eleven minutes at the gate is the time they start preferring the family whose gate opens. Agree the room, the table and the phone rule before the first session. Keep sessions where an adult is somewhere in the flat, with the door open, whatever the child's age.

Board claims tested by component, not by the name of the programme
Ask the tutor to mark a returned answer in front of you and explain it

sections.heading: Why does a 4.30pm lesson work in Seawoods when it does not in the island city?
paragraphs: Because the school gate and the flat are minutes apart. Seawoods is planned sector housing beside the Nerul campus cluster, so a child who leaves school a little before four is home, fed and at a table by half past, with the day still in working memory. That is not a scheduling nicety. It is the difference between reviewing today's lesson and excavating it. A parent in South Mumbai booking the same hour is asking a tutor to cross Peddar Road in the evening peak, and gets offered eight o'clock instead, by which point the child has forgotten which step of the method confused them.

Take a concrete case. A Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry student at Ryan Global School does the titration practical in a Thursday morning double period. She records burette readings, gets one titre that disagrees with the others, and hands the sheet in with a mean calculated from all three. At 4.30pm the same day her tutor has the raw sheet on the table and the practical is still vivid: she remembers that the third run was the one where she overshot the endpoint and the solution went dark pink. They discard the outlier, recalculate the mean from the concordant pair, fix the units in the table header, and work through the improvement question the paper always asks. Done two days later that conversation is guesswork, because the memory of the dark pink flask is gone and all that remains is a number.

The same logic applies right across both boards. An MYP Sciences student processing a graph the afternoon she collected the data still knows why one point sits off the line, which is exactly what Criterion C rewards. A Diploma Programme Physics student reviewing an internal assessment data run on the day can still go back and take two more readings before the equipment is packed away. A returned Mathematics test looked at the same evening gets corrected while the student still remembers what she was thinking; a week later she is reading her own working like a stranger's. Same-day review is the cheapest marks on the table and geography is what makes it possible.

There is a supply side to this too. A tutor whose evening route is Seawoods at 4.30pm, Nerul at six and CBD Belapur at half past seven is running a viable week, so the early slot is one they want rather than one they tolerate. The sector grid, the gated complexes with parking inside, and Palm Beach Road with few signals on it are the reasons that route holds. Ask for the slot. In this node it is an ordinary request, and anyone who tells you after-school tuition is impossible is quoting conditions from the other side of the creek.

Same-day practical review while the apparatus and the mistake are still vivid

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one Mumbai exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should see diagnosis and habit, not marks. By the end of the first month the tutor should be able to tell you in one sentence what is actually wrong, and it should be more specific than weak in Maths: she can factorise but does not recognise when a question wants it, or he knows the content and writes describe answers to evaluate questions. The visible change is procedural. Work gets done before the session rather than during it, a notebook exists, and corrections are written out instead of nodded at. We do not guarantee grades, and anyone in Navi Mumbai promising a number by a date is selling you something.

At one term, school assessment marks should start moving, and the movement is usually uneven. The subject where the problem was technique moves first, because command words are learnable in weeks. The subject where two years of foundations are missing moves last and may only steady rather than rise. Internal assessment drafts coming back from the school teacher with fewer structural comments is a strong signal, often stronger than a test score. By this point you should also be able to see the tutor's plan for the rest of the year, written down, pegged to the school's deadlines.

Across a full examination cycle you are looking for a grade that reflects what the student can do under timed conditions rather than what they know on a calm Sunday. That means mock papers sat properly, in the time allowed, marked against a mark scheme, with the lost marks categorised. Honest limits apply. Tuition cannot fix a level chosen wrongly in DP1, it cannot make up for a term of missed school, and it cannot help a student who will not write anything down. If one of those is the real problem, the right answer is a conversation with the school, not more hours.

One term: school marks moving unevenly, technique subjects first

sections.heading: Starting home classes in a Seawoods sector flat: what to have ready
paragraphs: Five things make the first session count, and all of them are already in your house. The last school report, with the teacher comments rather than only the grades. The school's assessment calendar for the year, including internal deadlines. Two or three pieces of marked work the child did badly on, uncorrected. The subject guide or syllabus for each subject in question, which the school will send if you ask. And a table with a chair, in a room with a door, not a bed and not the dining table during dinner.

Arrange the gate before the hour arrives. Tell your society office that a tutor will come weekly at a fixed time so the entry is routine, keep the parking sorted if they drive in off Palm Beach Road, and agree where phones go during the session. If the slot is 4.30pm, make sure your child eats something at four. A hungry fourteen-year-old at the end of a school day is not a student, and the tutor will spend the first twenty minutes of a paid hour on that instead of on Chemistry.

The first session itself is diagnostic and should look like one. Expect the tutor to read the marked work before teaching anything, ask your child to attempt a question while they watch the working rather than the answer, and finish with two or three things written down for the week. Expect a short conversation with you at the end, in plain language, about what they found and what they will do about it. Expect no promises about grades. Then book the second session for the same hour on the same day and let the rhythm do its work.

Get the subject guide or syllabus from the school for each subject

faqs.question: Can a home tutor really start at 4.30pm on a weekday in Seawoods?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the few parts of Mumbai where that is an ordinary request rather than a favour. Seawoods is planned sector housing beside the Nerul campus cluster, so the gap between the school gate and your door is minutes, not an hour in traffic. A tutor can then run a second lesson in Nerul and a third in CBD Belapur the same evening, which is why the early slot suits them commercially as well as suiting you. Say the hour you want in your first message. If no specialist in that subject has it free, we will say so rather than book you at nine and hope.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Seawoods depend on?
faqs.answer: Rates are set by the tutor, and we will not publish a figure that pretends otherwise. What moves them is predictable. Board and level come first: a Diploma Programme Higher Level science or Mathematics specialist costs more than a Year nine IGCSE generalist. Subject scarcity is next, and it is the biggest single factor for things like HL Economics, Computer Science or a second language. Then session length, how many sessions a week you book, and travel distance, which is mild inside the Navi Mumbai nodes and significant for a cross-creek match. Ask every shortlisted tutor for their rate in writing before the first session.

faqs.question: Our complex issues a visitor gate pass each time. How does that work for a weekly tutor?
faqs.answer: Register the tutor once with the society office as a regular weekly visitor instead of signing them in as a guest every week. Most gated complexes in Seawoods will add a recurring name and time to the register if a resident asks in writing, and some will issue a long-term pass. Do it in the first week, before the pattern of waiting at the gate sets in. Also check whether visitor parking is inside or outside the gate, because a tutor driving in off Palm Beach Road who cannot park reliably will quietly start preferring the family whose gate is simpler. These small things decide whether a slot survives a full term.

faqs.question: Will the tutor travel from Nerul or CBD Belapur, or does someone come from the island city?
faqs.answer: Almost always from inside the Navi Mumbai nodes. Tutors are matched node to node because Vashi, Nerul, Belapur, Kharghar and Panvel are each a short drive from the next on the Sion–Panvel Highway and Palm Beach Road, and because a cross-creek weekday commitment rarely lasts a whole term even with the Atal Setu open. A tutor from the Western Suburbs may keep it up for a few weeks and then start requesting weekends. If the only real specialist for your subject lives across the creek, we will offer them online or hybrid rather than pretend the drive is sustainable.

faqs.question: How do we judge the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Seawoods for our child?
faqs.answer: There is no single best tutor; there is the right match for one child, one subject and one hour of the week. Judge on four things. Component experience: have they taught this exact paper, tier or internal assessment, not just the subject. Diagnosis: after one session, can they name precisely what is going wrong. Reliability: will they hold a fixed weekday slot inside this node for a full term. And whether your child talks to them. Parents who type IB and IGCSE tutors near me into Google from a Seawoods flat are usually looking for the last two, not the first two, and both matter.

faqs.question: Does an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Seawoods work as well for a scarce subject?
faqs.answer: For a scarce subject it is often the better choice, and for a young child it rarely is. If your daughter needs HL Psychology, Computer Science or Spanish and the specialist with genuine component experience lives in Juhu or outside Mumbai, an online session with that person beats a home session with a generalist who is learning the syllabus alongside her. Diploma Programme students manage screen work well, particularly for essay and draft feedback. Below roughly MYP Year three, attention goes long before the hour does. The honest compromise is hybrid: home for teaching, online for drafting and review.

faqs.question: My child finishes at Ryan Global School before four. Is a same-day review better than a weekend session?
faqs.answer: For anything practical or recently marked, yes, clearly. A Chemistry titration reviewed at 4.30pm on the day it was done still has the detail in it: which run overshot, why one titre disagreed, what the flask actually looked like. By Saturday that is gone and the student is reasoning about a number on a page. The same holds for a returned test and for internal assessment data collection, where a same-day look can send the student back for two more readings. Weekends suit bulk revision, past papers under timed conditions and Extended Essay work. Most families here end up using both.

faqs.question: There has been no change after four weeks. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Ask for the diagnosis in one sentence, in writing, and judge the answer. At four weeks you should not expect marks to have moved, but you should expect precision: not she is weak in Physics but she can rearrange formulae and cannot read a question that hides the variable. If the tutor cannot produce that sentence, the sessions are tuition without a plan and a change is warranted. If they can, ask what the next four weeks will do about it and what you should see. Also check the dull possibilities first: sessions shortened, homework not done, a slot that keeps slipping.

faqs.question: The tutor is competent but my daughter has stopped talking in sessions. How does a change happen?
faqs.answer: Tell us, and the replacement comes from the same brief you already gave, so you are not starting over. A child who has gone silent is giving you real information and it is worth acting on quickly rather than waiting out a paid month. We ask for the specifics because they shape the next match: too fast, too harsh on errors, talks over her, or simply the wrong temperament for a quiet fifteen-year-old. The next shortlist is filtered on that. Keep the same weekday hour if you can, because the slot is the part that is hard to rebuild in Navi Mumbai.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both my children if one is in MYP and the other in IGCSE Year 11?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, but do not force it. Back-to-back sessions in one visit work well for a Mathematics or Science tutor comfortable across both boards, and they save a second gate entry and a second evening. Where it fails is at the top end: an IGCSE Year 11 Extended candidate three months from the examination series needs someone who knows that paper properly, and the MYP child's criterion work is a different job. A home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai does not exist. Two specialists on two evenings is usually the better arrangement.

faqs.question: What happens in the monsoon, or on an evening the Harbour Line is disrupted?
faqs.answer: The session moves online rather than being cancelled, and that is agreed with the tutor in the first week so nobody is negotiating in the rain. Seawoods–Darave is on the Harbour Line and most tutors inside these nodes drive or use Palm Beach Road, which holds up better than the island city routes, but July and August will still take an evening or two. The rule we suggest is simple: if the tutor cannot reach you, the hour still happens on a screen. Missed sessions should be made up within the same week, not banked vaguely for later.

sections.heading: How IB Gram matches a home tutor to a Seven Bungalows address
paragraphs: A request for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Seven Bungalows works best when it is specific about three things: the board, the year group, and where exactly you are. Seven Bungalows runs from the Andheri West end down to the sand at Versova, and whether a tutor can hold a 6pm slot depends on which end of that stretch you live at. Tell us the lane, the nearest landmark, and whether a car can stand outside your compound. The shortlist changes before it is even drawn up.

From there the matching is mechanical rather than mysterious. We filter by board and subject first, because a teacher who has run Cambridge International Education Physics for six years is not automatically ready for Diploma Programme (DP) Physics at Higher Level (HL), and the reverse is just as true. Then we filter by how the tutor travels. For an address here we deliberately move car-owning tutors up the list, because the single strongest argument for this pocket is that a tutor can drive in, park, and walk to your door without losing twenty minutes to a barrier and a visitor register.

What comes back is a short list, not a catalogue. Two or three profiles, each with the board taught, the subjects, the year groups, the travel time from where that tutor actually lives, and the evenings they have free. You read them, pick one, and take a trial session in your own living room rather than on a video call. If the fit is wrong after it, you say so and we move. No parent is asked to justify a gut feeling about who sits beside their child twice a week.

One thing we ask for up front, because it saves a fortnight: the child's last two assessment sheets, whatever they happen to be. A Middle Years Programme (MYP) criterion breakdown, an IGCSE mock paper with the examiner marks still on it, a DP predicted grade sheet. A tutor who sees real marks before the first visit arrives with a plan instead of a questionnaire.

sections.heading: Which programmes do families in Seven Bungalows actually need?
paragraphs: Four, mostly. The International Baccalaureate (IB) Primary Years Programme (PYP) in the junior years, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) from roughly Year 6 to Year 10, the International General Certificate of Secondary Education (IGCSE) across Years 9 to 11, and the IB Diploma Programme (DP) in the final two years. A handful of families here run Cambridge AS and A Level instead of the DP, and a few switch boards mid-school.

Those four are not variations on one thing. PYP work is inquiry-led and carries no external examination, so a PYP request is usually about reading fluency, number sense, or a child who has moved in from a CBSE or ICSE school and is lost inside a transdisciplinary unit. MYP is assessed against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight, with grade boundaries sitting on top of that, which is why MYP parents so often say the report card means nothing to them. The MYP Personal Project in the final MYP year is the first piece of long-form independent work most of these children have attempted.

IGCSE and the DP are the two that carry external papers, and they produce most requests for all IB and IGCSE subjects home classes in Seven Bungalows. IGCSE sets a Core and Extended entry choice in several subjects and a two-year syllabus ending in a May or June series, with a November series behind it for resits and staggered entries. The DP is six subjects, three at HL and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the Extended Essay (EE), Theory of Knowledge (TOK) and Creativity, Activity, Service. The core is where DP students lose the time nobody budgeted for.

Switching between these is more common in Andheri West than parents expect, usually at the end of MYP when a family moves a child from an IB continuum school to an IGCSE route, or the other way. Those transitions are a genuine tutoring need rather than a remedial one. A child who has only ever been marked on criteria has to learn what a mark scheme looks like, and a child who has only ever sat papers has to learn how to write a reflection that scores.

IGCSE: Core or Extended entry, May and June series, November resit series

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: what a Seven Bungalows parent decides
paragraphs: Most parents who ask for an all IB and IGCSE subjects home tutor in Seven Bungalows are not really asking about teaching yet. They are asking about a choice: whether the child sits IGCSE Mathematics 0580 at Core or at Extended, whether Chemistry goes HL or SL in the DP, whether Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation is the honest fit. Those decisions get made in a week and paid for over two years.

Take 0580. The Core paper set caps the available grade at C, and the Extended set opens A* but carries topics the Core tier never meets: functions and their inverses, the sine and cosine rules in non right-angled triangles, differentiation of simple polynomials, set notation past the basics. A child parked on Core in Year 9 after one weak term can discover in Year 11 that a DP Mathematics choice has quietly been made on their behalf. A tutor worth paying says this out loud in the first month rather than the last.

The DP attaches an Internal Assessment (IA) to every subject, and this is the part families underestimate. The Mathematics IA is an independent exploration of roughly twelve to twenty pages, marked against five criteria and worth a fifth of the subject grade. Each experimental science carries a scientific investigation worth the same share. History, Economics, Business Management, Psychology and the language subjects each have their own internally assessed piece with its own word limit and its own criteria. A DP2 student is drafting several of these in the same term as mock examinations.

IGCSE coursework is lighter but not absent. Cambridge Geography and Cambridge History offer coursework options, several sciences run a practical paper instead of coursework, and Cambridge English Literature can be entered with or without the coursework component depending on what the school chose. Ask the school which route your child was entered on before you ask a tutor to prepare for the other one. The teacher in charge of the subject will answer that in a two-line email, and it saves a term of misdirected work.

sections.heading: Versova, Four Bungalows and Andheri West: what one tutor covers in a Mumbai evening
paragraphs: A tutor who takes a Seven Bungalows family almost always takes two or three more inside the same arc: Versova on one side, Four Bungalows up towards the junction, and the wider Andheri West spread inland. These are ten and fifteen minute drives from each other off-peak. That is the only reason a parent searching for IB and IGCSE tutors near me in Seven Bungalows gets a usable shortlist at all. The tutor is not making the trip for your household alone.

The Western Suburbs of Mumbai run north to south along the Western Express Highway and the Western Line, and that geometry decides evening scheduling more than anything else. A tutor coming from Bandra to Andheri is quick off-peak and painful at 6pm. Matching along the line, Khar to Santacruz or Malad to Kandivali, works far better than matching across it. For Seven Bungalows the practical catchment is Andheri West, Versova, Four Bungalows, Juhu, Oshiwara and Goregaon West, with Link Road rather than the highway acting as the spine.

Versova station on Metro Line 1 sits a short ride away and matters mainly for tutors who do not drive. Four Bungalows has its own station on the same line. But the argument of this page is about the tutors who do drive, and for them the relevant geography is Link Road, JP Road, and the plain fact that the lanes off Seven Bungalows are wide enough to leave a car on. A tutor finishing at Four Bungalows at 5.30pm can be sitting in a Seven Bungalows living room by 5.50pm, which is not true of almost any cross-suburb pairing.

Mumbai, Maharashtra is a city where a twelve kilometre match looks fine on a map and collapses in week three. We would rather send a tutor from Andheri West or Versova who can hold the same Tuesday slot for eight months than a more decorated one from Chembur who starts asking to reschedule in August. Distance is not the measure. Repeatability is.

sections.heading: JBCN International School Oshiwara, Billabong High and the Mumbai school calendar
paragraphs: Children in Seven Bungalows are spread across several international schools rather than concentrated in one. JBCN International School, Oshiwara is the closest IB and IGCSE option and sits a short drive inland along Link Road. Billabong High International School draws families from Juhu, Santacruz and Andheri West. Others travel to Ecole Mondiale World School or Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, and a smaller number go as far as Oberoi International School on JVLR.

The calendar those schools keep is what actually sets tutoring demand in Mumbai. The academic year opens in June, settles through the monsoon, and produces its first serious assessments around August and September. December and January bring mock examinations. For DP2 the run from November to February is the hardest stretch of the two years: final IA submissions, the Extended Essay, the TOK essay and mocks all land inside roughly fourteen weeks. IGCSE candidates sit the May and June series, with the November series used for resits and early entries.

What that means for a home tutor in Seven Bungalows is that August and November are the two months when a weekly slot is hardest to secure, and April and May are when the pool opens again. Families who fix a tutor in June barely notice the calendar. Families who start looking in October discover that every DP Chemistry tutor on the shortlist is already committed on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and that the one remaining slot is a Saturday morning nobody in the house wants.

One line needs saying plainly rather than hiding in a footer: IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with JBCN International School, Oshiwara, Billabong High International School, or any other school named on this page. sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid in Seven Bungalows: which one holds for a full term?
paragraphs: Home tuition holds best here, and the reason is parking. Because Seven Bungalows stays low-rise and residential almost to the Versova beach end, a tutor who drives can leave the car on the lane and be upstairs in two minutes. In the tower clusters further inland that same tutor loses ten minutes to visitor parking and a gate register twice in one evening. Across a term that adds up to several hours of a working tutor's life, and tutors schedule accordingly.

So IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows is the default we recommend, and most families stay on it. The child works at their own desk with their own files. The tutor sees the textbook, the school diary and the half-finished IA on the same table instead of hearing about them. Nothing is lost to a camera angle, and a Physics problem gets sketched on paper that stays in the house afterwards for the student to find again on Sunday.

An IB and IGCSE online tutor in Seven Bungalows is still worth keeping in the mix, and in two situations it is the better option. The first is a scarce subject: DP Film, Global Politics, Japanese B, Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at HL for a student aiming very high. There may be a small number of people in the city who teach it properly and none of them lives within driving distance of Andheri West. The second is examination season, when a thirty minute doubt call on a Sunday night beats a rescheduled two hour visit.

Hybrid is where most families end up by March without ever deciding to. A weekly session at home, plus a short screen share when a draft needs reading before a Monday deadline. The honest trade-offs: online suits a self-starting DP student and fails a Year 7 child who needs a person sitting next to them; home classes cost the tutor travel and therefore cost you more per hour than the same tutor on a screen. Both of those are true at once and neither cancels the other.

sections.heading: How is an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Seven Bungalows checked before the first session?
paragraphs: Before a profile for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Seven Bungalows reaches you, we check government photo identity, the degree or teaching qualification being claimed, and the board experience being claimed. A tutor who says they have taught DP Economics for four years is asked which syllabus, which school, and which paper students lose the most marks on. Vague answers end the conversation there.

Driving tutors get one additional check, because this page is built on them: a valid licence and a vehicle they genuinely own or use, not a borrowed arrangement that evaporates in week four. It sounds pedantic written down. It is the whole difference between a tutor who reliably arrives at 7pm through August and one who begins asking to shift everything to Saturday mornings once the rain sets in.

What we cannot check is chemistry with your child, and that is what actually decides whether this works. So check it yourself in the trial session. Ask the tutor to mark one question from a past paper in front of you and talk through the mark scheme line by line. Ask which version of the syllabus your school is running. Ask what they would do in the first three weeks. A parent hunting for the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Seven Bungalows learns more from those three questions than from any profile ever written.

Ask about references, and ask for a current family rather than one from three years ago. A tutor who has been teaching across Andheri West and Versova for a while can produce one inside a day. The ones who cannot are usually new to it, which is not disqualifying on its own, but it should change what you pay and how long you wait before committing to a full term of weekly sessions.

sections.heading: Why a tutor with a car changes what is possible in Seven Bungalows
paragraphs: The lanes off Seven Bungalows stay low-rise and residential almost all the way to the sand at Versova. There are compounds and gates, but there is also kerb, and a tutor can leave a car on it without circling. That is a small fact with disproportionate consequences, because a car-based tutor is a different kind of tutor from a train-and-rickshaw one. The difference shows up in three places: what they can carry, how many families they can serve in one evening, and whether they turn up in July.

A tutor who drives in Mumbai is usually one of three people. A full-time professional tutor who has stopped teaching in a school. A serving teacher taking two evenings a week. Or an experienced former examiner who keeps a small number of DP students. All three are further along than the typical part-time graduate, and all three live somewhere they can keep a vehicle, which in the Western Suburbs means Malad, Goregaon, Andheri or Bandra rather than a shared flat beside a station. Matching an IB and IGCSE private tutor in Seven Bungalows out of that group is realistic here in a way it is not in parts of Mumbai where nobody can park.

Here is where it shows in the actual work. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, asks candidates to read instruments, build a results table, plot a graph and criticise a method they have only ever seen described on paper. Students lose marks in the same four places every single year: units written into the table body instead of the column heading, significant figures that drift between rows, a line of best fit dragged through the first and last points, and a conclusion that restates the data rather than evaluating the method. A tutor who drives arrives with a metre rule, a thermometer, a stopwatch, a spring and a set of slotted masses in the boot, and the student spends forty minutes measuring extension against load before writing a single table. A tutor arriving by train brings a phone and a printed question. The second lesson is not worthless. It is simply a different lesson, and Paper 6 rewards the first one.

Scheduling and weather are the other two advantages. A driving tutor can hold a 4.30pm in Four Bungalows and a 7pm in Seven Bungalows on the same evening, which means your slot is not the one sacrificed the moment they take on another family. Through the monsoon, from late June into September, a tutor with a car cancels far less often than one swapping from a train at Andheri to a rickshaw through standing water. The honest limit is worth stating: on an examination-week Friday, Link Road does not care what anybody drives, and a tutor crossing from the Eastern Suburbs will still arrive late.

sections.heading: What does progress look like after four weeks with a home tutor?
paragraphs: After four weeks, expect method rather than marks. The child should be laying out working the way a mark scheme wants it, bringing specific questions instead of saying everything is fine, and no longer freezing at the opening line of an unfamiliar problem. If a class test score has already moved, treat it as luck and do not build on it. Four weeks is not an examination cycle and nothing durable has been tested yet.

After one term you should be able to see it in school assessment. For IGCSE that means a mock or an end-of-term paper in the same format as the real thing. For MYP it means criterion scores that have moved on the criteria the tutor actually targeted, which is usually Criterion C and Criterion D before Criterion A. For DP it means a predicted grade conversation less tense than the last one, and an IA with a research question the subject teacher has genuinely approved rather than tolerated.

After one full examination cycle you can judge properly. A year of weekly work with a competent IB and IGCSE tutor in Mumbai moves most students a band, and occasionally two where the starting point was a gap in foundations rather than ability. But IB Gram does not guarantee grades, and no tutor who claims to should be allowed through your door. Too much sits outside anybody's control: illness in April, a subject the child quietly dislikes, a school that changes teachers halfway through DP2.

Tell us early if it is not working. The reliable warning signs are a child who stops doing the between-session work, a tutor who talks to you more than to the child, and four weeks of sessions that keep circling the same chapter. Replacement is a message, not a negotiation, and nobody will ask you to sit through one more session to be sure. We would far rather move a tutor in week five than read a complaint in March about a term already lost.

sections.heading: Starting IB and IGCSE home tuition in Seven Bungalows: what to have ready
paragraphs: Four documents make the first session with an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Seven Bungalows useful instead of exploratory: the most recent report card, the last test or mock paper with the marks still written on it, the school subject guide or syllabus code, and any IA or coursework brief with its deadline on it. Photographs taken on a phone are fine. A tutor who reads those before arriving opens with a plan rather than an interview.

Set the space up before the tutor arrives. A table rather than a bed, a second chair at the same table rather than a seat across the room, decent light, and the phone in another room. Most homes in Seven Bungalows have a corner that works, which is one more quiet advantage of low-rise living over a two-bedroom flat eleven floors up. Give your watchman the tutor's name and vehicle number once, and the Tuesday arrival stops being a conversation every week.

The first session is a diagnostic and it should look slightly slow. The tutor will push the child through problems a little above their comfort level to find where the floor actually is, ask what the school is covering this fortnight, and probably set something small for the next visit. You should get a short written note afterwards saying what they found. Read that note carefully, because it tells you whether the tutor understood your child or is running a standard script they use everywhere.

Be in the house for the first session at least. You do not need to sit in, and most children work worse when a parent is watching from the doorway. But being around for the first one lets you hear the tone, see whether the child relaxes after ten minutes, and ask two real questions at the door on the way out. After that, a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects in Mumbai works perfectly well with a grandparent or house help at home.

faqs.question: What does an IB or IGCSE home tutor in Seven Bungalows cost?
faqs.answer: It depends on five things, and nobody honest will quote a flat rate before knowing them. IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Seven Bungalows move with the board and level, because DP Higher Level work asks more of a tutor than MYP does; with subject scarcity, since DP Chemistry and Further Mathematics have far fewer qualified teachers than English; with how far the tutor drives to reach your lane; with session length and weekly frequency; and with the tutor's own track record. Ask for the rate per session, the session length, and whether travel is included, in that order, before you agree to anything.

faqs.question: Can a tutor actually park near my building in Seven Bungalows?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the main practical reason tutors like this pocket. Seven Bungalows stays low-rise almost all the way to the Versova beach, so there is kerb space on most lanes and compound parking in many buildings, which is simply not the case in the tower clusters towards Lokhandwala. Tell us at the matching stage whether your building lets a visitor car inside the gate or whether the tutor should park on the road. It takes one line in your first message and it removes the single most common source of first-week friction.

faqs.question: What happens if the tutor is not working out after three or four sessions?
faqs.answer: You tell us and we replace them, usually inside a week. There is no argument and no requirement to write an essay about it, although specifics help the next match: too fast, too slow, no structure, no rapport. We ask only that you say it in week four rather than month four. A replacement in Seven Bungalows tends to be quicker than in most of Mumbai, because Versova, Four Bungalows and Andheri West form one catchment, so the second tutor is drawn from the same set of people who can already reach your door on a weekday.

faqs.question: Will a tutor travel to Seven Bungalows for a 7pm weekday slot?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and more easily than in many parts of Mumbai. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Seven Bungalows driving in from Andheri West, Four Bungalows, Versova or Juhu is covering a short run on Link Road rather than crossing the city. The 7pm slot is the hardest to fill anywhere because it collides with the evening peak, and what does not work reliably is 6pm for a tutor coming down from Malad or up from Bandra, since that is the worst hour on the Western Express Highway. Ask for 7.15pm and the shortlist gets noticeably longer.

faqs.question: Does online tuition really work for IB Diploma Programme subjects?
faqs.answer: For a motivated DP student, yes; for a struggling Year 7, rarely. Online suits work that is already written down: reviewing an Internal Assessment draft, walking through a past paper the student has already attempted, a short doubt call the night before a test. It fails when a child needs somebody physically present to stop them drifting, or when the subject needs apparatus and sketching on shared paper. Most families here settle on weekly sessions at home with occasional online top-ups during mock and examination weeks, which is a sensible compromise rather than a failure of either mode.

faqs.question: My child is already in DP2 and the Internal Assessment deadlines have started. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: No, but the plan shifts from teaching to triage. In DP2 the realistic order is: meet the IA deadlines the school has set, because those marks are banked and cannot be recovered afterwards; then work backwards through past papers by topic instead of teaching the syllabus in sequence; then fix examination technique in the final six weeks before the May session. A tutor who starts a DP2 student in November by returning to the first unit of the course is spending months you no longer have. Say so in the trial session if they suggest it.

faqs.question: What happens to an evening session during the Mumbai monsoon?
faqs.answer: Less disruption than you would expect, provided your tutor drives. Between late June and September the tutors who cancel most are the ones swapping from a train at Andheri to a rickshaw through standing water. A car-based tutor loses the occasional session to a genuinely flooded stretch and otherwise arrives late rather than not at all. We ask every tutor to agree a make-up rule with the family in advance: same week, one fixed alternative evening, or a credited session. Settle that in July when it is theoretical, not in August when everyone is annoyed.

faqs.question: Do I need to be at home during the session?
faqs.answer: Not after the first one. Be present for session one so you can hear how the tutor speaks to your child and ask questions at the door afterwards. After that an adult in the house is enough, and plenty of families here run sessions with a grandparent or house help around. What matters more than supervision is the setup: a proper table, decent light, the phone somewhere else, and a door that can be shut if younger siblings are in the flat. Children work differently when a parent is watching, and in most cases they work worse.

faqs.question: Do you cover Versova, Four Bungalows and Andheri West with the same tutors?
faqs.answer: Yes, that is precisely how the pool is built. A tutor matched to Seven Bungalows is almost always already teaching one or two families in Versova, Four Bungalows or the wider Andheri West area, which is what makes a dependable weekly slot possible in the first place. Versova station on Metro Line 1 and the Four Bungalows station serve the tutors who do not drive. For the ones who do, the whole arc is about fifteen minutes end to end off-peak, and we work hard to keep every match inside it rather than dragging somebody across Mumbai.

faqs.question: Which schools do children in Seven Bungalows usually attend?
faqs.answer: Mostly JBCN International School, Oshiwara and Billabong High International School, with families also travelling to Ecole Mondiale World School and Jamnabai Narsee International School in Juhu, and a smaller number to Oberoi International School on JVLR. It matters for tutoring because of the calendar: these schools set mocks, IA deadlines and reporting windows at slightly different times, so a tutor already teaching a child at your school knows which fortnight is about to get difficult. IB Gram is an independent platform and is not affiliated with any of the schools mentioned.

faqs.question: How do I choose between home tuition and a group coaching class?
faqs.answer: Decide by what is actually wrong. If the problem is one specific gap, a shaky grasp of moles in IGCSE Chemistry or a Mathematics IA with no workable research question, one-to-one work at your own table fixes it faster than any class can. If the child is broadly fine and simply needs drilled practice at a peer pace, a class is reasonable and costs less. What a group class cannot do is adapt to an MYP criterion breakdown or read your child's half-written Extended Essay. Most families here use home tuition for the two hardest subjects and leave the rest alone.

sections.heading: How we match an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sewri to your child
paragraphs: A request from Sewri usually arrives as four lines: the grade, the board, the subject that has gone sideways, and the two evenings that are actually free. Our job is to turn that into two or three names you can choose between, not a directory of forty profiles. Sewri is a compact catchment, so we open with a question that matters more here than it would in Andheri or Thane: which direction should the tutor come from? Until recently the honest answer was the island city, which in practice meant Parel, Lower Parel, Wadala, Dadar and Byculla. That is still the answer for most weekday bookings. The Atal Setu has added a second one, and for a handful of scarce subjects it is the difference between a specialist and a compromise. Either way, what you are booking is an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sewri who can hold one fixed weekly slot for a whole term.

The sequence is deliberately short. 1. You send the grade, board, subject and the two or three weekly windows that genuinely work, including whether a weekend morning is possible. 2. Distance is a scheduling constraint, not a qualification. We weight it that way, and we tell you which of the two you are trading off before you book rather than after the third cancelled session. Parents in this part of the island are used to being sold proximity. Proximity is cheap to supply and it is the first thing to stop mattering once the syllabus gets technical.

One more question we ask early: is this a term-long repair or a six-week push before mocks? The answer changes the match completely. A six-week push before an IGCSE series needs someone who already knows the paper structure cold, can walk in and start marking past questions in session one, and will not spend a fortnight building rapport. A term-long rebuild for a Year 9 student who lost ground two years ago in algebra needs patience, a slower diagnostic and a tolerance for going backwards before going forwards. Those are different teachers. Conflating them is the most common reason a family in Sewri ends up on their third tutor by November, and it is avoidable in the first phone call.

sections.heading: Which programme is your child actually in: PYP, MYP, DP or IGCSE?
paragraphs: Four pathways turn up in Sewri homes. The International Baccalaureate (IB) runs the Primary Years Programme (PYP) up to Year 5, the Middle Years Programme (MYP) across Years 6 to 10, and the Diploma Programme (DP) in Years 11 and 12. Running alongside them is IGCSE, usually taken in Years 9 and 10 under Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel. Which one your child sits in decides what a tutor should be doing in the room, and parents get this wrong more often than you would expect.

MYP and IGCSE look similar from the outside and behave nothing alike. MYP reports against four criteria per subject, each scored out of eight, with command terms that carry fixed expectations: describe, explain, evaluate and justify are not interchangeable, and a student who writes a beautiful description where the criterion asked for an evaluation has simply not answered. There are no percentages and no paper codes to drill. IGCSE, by contrast, is a timed written examination with a published mark scheme, and preparation is largely about the mark scheme. A tutor who treats an MYP Year 9 student as though they were sitting Cambridge papers will produce a child who is fluent at a test nobody is going to set them.

The Diploma Programme is a different machine again: six subjects, three at Higher Level (HL) and three at Standard Level (SL), plus the Core, which is Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service (CAS). The Core is where strong students lose points quietly, because it has no weekly homework to flag that it is slipping. A DP1 student in Sewri who has not chosen an Extended Essay subject by the end of the first year has a problem that will surface in October of DP2, when the first full draft is due at the same time as the mocks.

IGCSE adds its own fork: Core versus Extended tiers in several subjects, with a grade ceiling on Core that a parent should understand before the school's deadline for tier entry passes. Cambridge and Edexcel differ in paper structure, in how coursework is handled and in which series they run. A teacher who can hold all IB and IGCSE subjects across IB and IGCSE Years 1-12 is the one tutor Mumbai parents keep asking for, and the honest reply is that no such person exists. You want a tutor who owns two or three subjects properly and says so plainly about the rest.

sections.heading: Subject choice, HL and SL, Core and Extended: what each decision carries
paragraphs: Subject choice is the single highest-leverage decision in both boards, and it is usually made in a rush. In the Diploma Programme the question is not which subjects your child likes but which three they can survive at Higher Level while the Extended Essay and Internal Assessments stack up in the same months. At IGCSE the question is tier and combination: whether a student takes Coordinated Sciences or three separate sciences changes the weekly load for two years. A good tutor will tell you when a choice is wrong before the school's deadline, not console you about it in February.

Here is a worked example of the kind of thing a home tutor in Sewri should be doing. Take IGCSE Geography, syllabus 0460, and Paper 4, the Alternative to Coursework. Candidates are given a fieldwork scenario and asked to write a hypothesis, choose and justify a sampling method, read somebody else's collected data, and then evaluate the reliability of the whole exercise and suggest improvements. Students lose marks on the last two parts almost every time, because school teaching concentrates on the content and not on the method. A tutor sitting in a Sewri flat can do something no worksheet does: take the student out mentally onto the dock road below, design a pedestrian and vehicle count along the stretch towards the Sewri mudflats, decide between systematic and stratified sampling and say why, then write the limitation paragraph that a Paper 4 question will ask for, which is almost always about time of day, sample size and observer bias. One real example built on ground the child knows is worth six past papers of the same question answered from memory.

The same logic carries across the rest of the subject list. A DP Mathematics student, whether on Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, has to produce an Exploration with a genuine personal angle and a defensible mathematical process, not a survey dressed up with a graph. A DP Physics Internal Assessment stands or falls on uncertainty treatment and on whether the research question was narrow enough to be answered in the available lab time. A DP Business Management student has to work from real organisational material rather than invented figures. English Language and Literature students need their analytical paragraphs restructured, not just corrected. These are different skills, and asking one person to teach all of them well is asking for a generalist.

So when a parent in Sewri says they want a home tutor for all IB and IGCSE subjects Mumbai agencies cheerfully promise, we say the useful version of that: one platform, several specialists, scheduled so that your child is not sitting with four different people on four nights. In practice most families run one main tutor for the subject that is actually failing and add a second only when a second subject starts producing the same warning signs. Two tutors is manageable. Four is a timetable that collapses by the end of the term.

sections.heading: Sewri, Wadala, Mazgaon and Parel: who can reach your door, and when
paragraphs: Sewri sits on the eastern dockland edge of Mumbai, Maharashtra, between the port land and the mudflats, with Sewri station on the Harbour Line running CSMT to Dockyard Road to Sewri, and the Sewri–Wadala corridor carrying most of the local road traffic north. The Eastern Freeway runs overhead on its way down to the Fort end of the island, and the Atal Setu, formally the Mumbai Trans Harbour Link, lands here at the eastern edge. On the western side of the island, the Coastal Road and Metro Line 3 serve the Worli and Cuffe Parade to BKC axis, which is a different world for scheduling purposes even though it is only a few kilometres away.

A tutor matched to Sewri will normally also cover Wadala, Mazgaon and Parel, and that cluster is the practical catchment rather than a marketing radius. Wadala, just north along the corridor, is where many tutors actually live, and it is the easiest inbound trip of the three. Parel, with its hospital and office belt, is a short hop but can be slow between six and eight in the evening when the offices empty. Mazgaon, to the south, is close on the map and awkward in practice because of the dock road and the one-way patterns around it. A tutor who tells you they cover all of Sewri, Wadala, Mazgaon and Parel without hesitating has usually not driven it at seven in the evening.

The island-wide travel reality is worth stating plainly because it governs who we will offer you. South Mumbai is dense and short in distance but genuinely slow: a tutor crossing from Worli to Colaba covers about eight kilometres and can still lose forty minutes to the Peddar Road and Haji Ali signals in the evening peak. That is why tutors for this part of Mumbai are matched within the island rather than brought down from the suburbs. Someone living in Borivali who says they will teach in Sewri on a Tuesday evening is telling you about their intentions, not their commute, and that arrangement fails in week five.

Within that frame, IB and IGCSE home tuition in Sewri works best when the tutor's own base is one of the four areas in the cluster or directly on the corridor. sections.heading: How do the school calendars around Sewri and central Mumbai set the pressure points?
paragraphs: The international school year here starts in late July or August and the pressure arrives in three waves: October and November for mocks and the first serious internal deadlines, January and February for Internal Assessment final submissions and the Extended Essay, and April and May for the Diploma Programme examinations and the IGCSE May and June series. Families who start tutoring in December are usually starting in the middle of the second wave, which is the worst month to begin anything.

JBCN International School, Parel is the school most Sewri families name first, for the obvious reason that it is the nearest full IB and IGCSE campus and the drive is short enough to be done twice a day without the child losing an hour to it. Its calendar is the one that sets the rhythm for a lot of households in this cluster: when its assessment week lands, the requests we get from Sewri, Wadala and Parel spike together. A tutor who already teaches two or three students at the same campus will know which fortnight is going to be brutal before the parent does.

Bombay International School, over at the Babulnath end of the island, pulls in the other direction. Families who send a child there are already absorbing a daily cross-island commute, which compresses the usable evening at both ends. For those households the practical consequence is that a weekday session rarely starts before seven, and a tutor who needs to be somewhere else at eight is not a real option. We would rather tell you that at the matching stage than let you discover it. Several families in this position end up moving one of their two weekly sessions to Saturday morning simply to get a session where nobody is watching the clock.

To be explicit about what naming those schools does and does not mean: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and is not affiliated with JBCN International School, Parel, Bombay International School, or any other school mentioned on this page. We name them because that is where families in this part of Mumbai actually send their children, and because their calendars decide when the work gets hard. We have no arrangement with any of them, we do not place tutors through them, and no tutor on our platform should ever claim otherwise to you.

sections.heading: Home tuition, online or hybrid: which one fits a Sewri family?
paragraphs: Home tuition is the default here and it is what most parents in Sewri are searching for, because it removes the travel problem from the child and puts it on the adult who is being paid for their time. An IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sewri arrives at your flat, works at your dining table, sees the actual state of the folder and the notebook, and cannot be half-attended to behind a browser tab. For anyone below Year 10, and for any student whose core problem is working habits rather than content, that physical presence is doing most of the work.

Online is not a lesser option, it is a different one, and it wins in two specific cases. The first is scarcity: if your child needs Higher Level Economics, Computer Science, Spanish, or Environmental Systems and Societies, the number of experienced teachers within reach of the island is small, and an IB and IGCSE online tutor in Sewri who genuinely knows the syllabus beats a nearby generalist every time. The second is marking-heavy work. Reviewing an Extended Essay draft or a Theory of Knowledge outline on a shared screen, with the tutor annotating live, is arguably better than two heads over one printed page. Where online struggles is the student who needs somebody in the room to stop them drifting, and no amount of software fixes that.

Hybrid is the arrangement that suits this particular catchment, and it is worth setting up deliberately rather than falling into. The pattern that holds is one in-person session on a weekend morning or an early weekday evening, used for diagnosis, marking and anything practical, plus one shorter online session midweek for follow-up and homework review. It means the in-person slot is never the one fighting the worst hour of traffic. We arrange all IB and IGCSE subjects as home classes Sewri parents book week by week, and the hybrid version of the same arrangement keeps the tutor's travel inside the hours that actually work.

On the money side, mode changes what you are quoted. In-person home tutoring carries the tutor's travel time, and travel time in this part of Mumbai is not trivial even over short distances. Online carries none of it. Hybrid sits between the two. Nothing else about the teaching changes, so if a tutor quotes you a large premium for online, ask what it is for. The reasonable conversation is about the tutor's experience, the level being taught, and how long the session runs, not about the medium.

sections.heading: How is an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sewri checked before the first session?
paragraphs: Every tutor is checked on four things before a profile is shown to a Sewri family: government photo identity, the degree or teaching qualification claimed, demonstrable experience of the specific board and level, and references from families or schools they have worked with. Board experience is verified by conversation rather than by a certificate, because the certificate does not exist. We ask which syllabus codes they have taught, which session they last prepared students for, and how they would mark a specific criterion. Vague answers end the process.

Experience claims are where most of the filtering happens. There is a large difference between a teacher who has taught Physics and a teacher who has taken Diploma Programme Physics students through an Internal Assessment, and a far larger one between somebody who has read an IGCSE syllabus and somebody who has marked to its mark scheme. We also ask about the age range. A tutor who is excellent with DP2 students is often impatient with a Year 7 student who needs the question read aloud twice, and that mismatch shows up in week two as a child who has gone quiet.

There is also a set of checks only you can run, and you should run them in the trial session rather than taking our word for it. Ask the tutor which syllabus and which paper your child's next assessment is on, and listen for whether the answer is specific. Ask them to explain one marking criterion in plain language. Ask what they would do differently if your child were on Core rather than Extended. Then watch your child during the session: a student who is asking questions by minute twenty is in the right room, and a student who has stopped talking is not, whatever the credentials say.

Finally, a practical point about identity on the doorstep. When families type IB and IGCSE tutors near me Sewri into a search box and book through a classifieds listing, nobody has verified anything and no one is accountable when a person who is not the person in the photograph turns up. An IB and IGCSE private tutor Sewri families book through us is on record with us, is known to us by name and document, and the booking is traceable. If a tutor ever arrives and does not match the profile you were sent, you do not let them in and you tell us the same day.

sections.heading: What the Atal Setu changed for Sewri: a tutor pool that now runs east
paragraphs: Sewri is now the island-city end of the Atal Setu, and the practical result for parents is one almost nobody has thought about: a tutor living in Nerul or Vashi is, for the first time, a realistic option for a family here. Two years ago no household on this side of the harbour would have considered it. Every other locality on the island widens its tutor search north, towards Dadar and the central suburbs, or south towards Fort. Sewri is the one place in Mumbai where the sensible third direction is east, straight across the water.

This matters because of what sits on the other side. Navi Mumbai has its own developed international school ecosystem, with campuses such as D.Y. Patil International School in Nerul running IB and IGCSE for years now, which means there is a genuine population of experienced Diploma Programme and IGCSE teachers living in Vashi, Nerul, Belapur and Kharghar. Those teachers were effectively invisible to a Sewri parent before, not because they were far in kilometres but because the old route around the creek through Chembur and Vashi made a weekday evening lesson impossible to sustain. The bridge did not create those tutors. It made them bookable. For a parent hunting Higher Level Economics, Computer Science, a second modern language, or Environmental Systems and Societies, that is a real widening of a pool that was always thin on the island.

Now the honest part, because this is where families get it wrong. The crossing is genuinely quick, but the direction of travel at the wrong hour is not symmetrical with how it looks on a map. A tutor who finishes a session in Sewri at seven on a Tuesday is starting a return leg into the thick of the evening, and the approach roads at either end are what cost the time, not the bridge itself. Ask a Navi Mumbai tutor to hold a 7.30pm weekday slot across the harbour every week and the arrangement will survive about a month before the cancellations start. What does hold is a weekend morning, when the road is empty in both directions, or an early weekday slot that finishes before the peak builds. Book the hour, not the optimism.

So the practical advice for a family hiring an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sewri is this. If the subject you need is available on the island, take the island tutor and keep your weekday evening. If it is not, widen east deliberately: ask which node the tutor lives in, agree a weekend or early-evening slot from the start, and agree in writing a fixed online fallback for the weeks when something goes wrong at either end. Parents ask us who the best IB and IGCSE tutor in Sewri is, and the real answer is whichever qualified specialist can hold the same slot for a full term. Since the bridge opened, that person is sometimes somebody with a Navi Mumbai address, which is a sentence nobody in this part of Mumbai could have written before.

sections.heading: What progress looks like at four weeks, one term and one exam cycle
paragraphs: At four weeks you should not be looking at grades, and any tutor who points at a grade after four weeks is pointing at noise. What you should see is narrower and more reliable: homework that is finished before the session rather than during it, a child who can explain the method back to you rather than just producing an answer, fewer blank starts on a question, and a tutor who can tell you specifically what the gap is. If after four weekly sessions nobody can name the actual problem in one sentence, the match is not working and the subject is not the reason.

At one term, meaning roughly three months, a full assessment cycle has gone past. There has been a school test or a mock, an Internal Assessment draft has been submitted somewhere, and there is real evidence to look at. This is the point to ask for the comparison honestly: not whether the number went up, but whether the kind of mistake changed. A student who used to lose marks for not answering the question and now loses them for an arithmetic slip has improved substantially, even if the mark is similar. A student making exactly the same category of error in December as in September has not, and three more months of the same will not fix it.

Across one full examination cycle the picture is clearer still, and so are the limits. We do not guarantee grades, and anybody in this city who does is either lying or has not been doing this long. What a tutor controls is preparation, feedback quality, deadline discipline and the number of past papers that get properly marked rather than just completed. What a tutor does not control is how the child sleeps in April, how the school paces the syllabus, what comes up on the paper, or whether a student who has been coasting for two years decides in February to start. Progress is a probability shifted, not an outcome bought.

Which brings us to when to stop. If two terms have gone by with a tutor your child likes, attendance is good, and the category of error has not changed at all, the right move is usually a different teacher rather than more hours with the same one. We would rather arrange that than keep a booking alive. Equally, if the subject is fine and the real problem is that a DP1 student is doing six subjects badly because they have no working method, more subject tuition is the wrong purchase and we will say so.

One term: the category of error should have changed, not just the mark

sections.heading: Starting home classes in Sewri: what to have ready for the first session
paragraphs: Have five things ready and the first session is worth double. The most recent school report, the last two marked test papers including the ones with poor marks, the subject guide or syllabus code, any Internal Assessment brief with its real school deadline, and a decision about where the session happens. That last one matters more than parents expect: a dining table with a chair at the right height beats a bedroom every time, and a child working from a bed has already told you how the session will go.

The first session itself is diagnostic and should feel like it. A good tutor spends the opening part working out what the student can actually do rather than what the syllabus says they should be able to do, usually by setting a short piece of work and watching where it breaks. By the end of that session you should get a plain summary: this is the gap, this is what we do for the next four weeks, this is what I need from the student between sessions. If you get a summary that would fit any child in Mumbai, ask a sharper question before you book the second one.

On cost, we will not publish a price list, because a single figure would be wrong for most of the people reading it. What IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Sewri depend on is straightforward and worth knowing before you ask: the board and level, since Diploma Programme Higher Level work commands more than MYP; subject scarcity, since Higher Level Economics or Computer Science has a thinner supply than Mathematics; the tutor's own experience and examining background; travel distance and time, which is why a cross-harbour weekend slot and a Wadala weekday slot are not priced identically; and session length and weekly frequency. Ask for a quote against your actual requirement rather than a general rate, and ask whether it is per session or per hour, because those are not the same conversation.

One practical note on access, because it causes more missed first sessions than anything else. Most buildings in and around Sewri want a visitor entry, a phone call to the flat, or a pre-registered name at the gate. Tell us the building protocol when you book and we pass it to the tutor, or better, register the tutor as a recurring visitor for the standing slot once the trial has gone well. An IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai families book for a full term should not be standing at your gate every week explaining who they are.

faqs.question: How quickly can you find an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sewri?
faqs.answer: Most requests for an IB and IGCSE home tutor in Sewri are filled within two to four working days, and scarce subjects take longer. Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Economics and English at both boards move fastest because the supply across the island city is reasonable. Higher Level Economics, Computer Science, Environmental Systems and Societies and second languages can take a week or more, and that is when we look east across the Atal Setu rather than keep you waiting. The other variable is your slot: a 5pm weekday request fills faster than a 7.30pm one, because the evening peak thins the pool of tutors who can honestly commit.

faqs.question: What do IB and IGCSE tuition fees in Sewri depend on?
faqs.answer: Five things, and no honest platform can quote you a figure without knowing them. The board and level come first, since Diploma Programme Higher Level teaching is priced above MYP or primary work. Then subject scarcity: a thin supply of qualified teachers in a subject raises the rate regardless of anything else. Then the tutor's own experience and whether they have examining or marking background. Then travel, because a tutor giving up ninety minutes of evening road time is pricing that in. Then session length and how many sessions a week you want. Ask for a quote against your specific requirement, not a published rate.

faqs.question: Will a tutor from Navi Mumbai really come across the Atal Setu every week?
faqs.answer: For a weekend morning or an early weekday evening, yes, and those arrangements hold for a full term. For a 7.30pm weekday session, be sceptical. The crossing itself is fast, but the return leg at that hour runs into the worst of the evening on the approach roads, and a tutor from Nerul or Vashi who agrees to it enthusiastically in September tends to start cancelling by October. We would rather set up a Saturday slot that survives the year. If a cross-harbour tutor is the right subject specialist, agree the hour carefully and agree an online fallback in advance.

faqs.question: Can a tutor get into our building in Sewri without a problem at the gate?
faqs.answer: Yes, provided you tell us the protocol when you book. Buildings around Sewri, Wadala and Parel vary: some want a phone call to the flat, some want a visitor pass with photo identity, some want the resident to pre-register a recurring visitor. Tell us which applies and we brief the tutor before the first visit, including the name they should give and whether there is a specific gate. After the trial session has gone well, register the tutor as a standing weekly visitor. It takes one conversation with your society office and removes five minutes of friction from every subsequent session.

faqs.question: Does a parent need to be at home during home tuition?
faqs.answer: For the trial session, yes, and for younger children, generally yes. For the first session we ask that an adult is present at least for the start, both for your own comfort and because you learn more in those twenty minutes about the tutor than from any profile. After that it depends on age: for PYP and lower MYP students an adult in the flat is sensible, while most DP students work better without a parent in earshot. Many families in Sewri settle on an adult at home but in another room, which is usually the right balance between supervision and letting the session breathe.

faqs.question: What happens if a session is missed because of traffic or heavy rain?
faqs.answer: It gets rescheduled, not charged, provided the tutor could not reasonably make it. Monsoon weeks in this part of Mumbai genuinely disrupt road travel, and the dockland approach roads and the Eastern Freeway ramps are not immune. The standing rule we ask tutors to follow is to tell you by early afternoon if the evening looks impossible, rather than at 6.45pm. In most cases the session moves online the same evening rather than being lost, which is why we suggest agreeing an online fallback at the time of booking instead of improvising one in the middle of a downpour.

faqs.question: Does online tuition actually work for IB Internal Assessments?
faqs.answer: For Internal Assessments it often works better than in-person, which surprises people. Internal Assessment supervision is mostly reading drafts, annotating them, and arguing about the research question, and all of that is easier on a shared screen where both people see the same document and the comments persist afterwards. Where online is weaker is practical work, diagram-heavy explanation on the fly, and any student who needs somebody physically present to stay on task. A common and sensible split for a Sewri family is in-person for the subject teaching and online for the draft review cycles in January and February.

faqs.question: The tutor is good but it is not working after three weeks. What now?
faqs.answer: Tell us and we re-match, with no argument and no pressure to persist. Teaching fit is not a judgement on either party: a tutor who is excellent with a methodical DP2 student can be wrong for a Year 8 who needs the question read aloud twice. When you write in, tell us what specifically is not landing, because that is what makes the second match better than the first. Pace too fast, no structure to the session, the child has gone quiet, too much lecturing and not enough work done in the room: each of those points at a different replacement.

faqs.question: There is no visible progress after a month. Should we be worried?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but you should be asking a sharper question. After four weeks the right test is not the mark but whether anyone can name the gap in one sentence and whether the kind of error has started to change. If the tutor can tell you exactly what is wrong and what the next four weeks address, that is progress even without a better score. If a month in nobody can say what the problem is, the diagnosis never happened and more sessions will not produce one. That is the point to ask for a different tutor rather than wait for a second term.

faqs.question: My child is at JBCN International School, Parel. Do your tutors know that calendar?
faqs.answer: Many do, because it is the nearest IB and IGCSE campus to Sewri and a large share of local requests come from families there. A tutor already working with students at the same campus will usually know the assessment weeks and the internal submission dates before you mention them, which matters most in October and January. To be clear about the relationship: IB Gram is independent and has no affiliation with the school, and a tutor's familiarity with its calendar comes from teaching students who attend it, nothing more. Tell us the campus when you write in and we factor it into the shortlist.

faqs.question: We live nearer Wadala or Mazgaon than Sewri station. Does that change the match?
faqs.answer: It changes the pool, usually in your favour. Wadala sits on the corridor where a lot of tutors actually live, so a Wadala-end address often widens the shortlist and shortens the inbound trip. Mazgaon is closer to Sewri on the map but slower in practice because of the dock road and the one-way pattern around it, so we tend to look south and west for that side. Either way, send your actual location and the nearest landmark rather than just the pin code, because in this cluster a kilometre in the wrong direction changes which tutors can realistically hold a weekday evening.

sections.heading: Which programme is your child actually in: PYP, MYP, DP or IGCSE?
paragraphs: Four systems sit behind the word tuition in Mumbai: the International Baccalaureate (IB) Primary Years Programme (PYP), the Middle Years Programme (MYP) for Years 1 to 5, IGCSE for Years 9 to 11 under Cambridge International Education or Pearson Edexcel, and the IB Diploma Programme (DP) for the final two years. A tutor who is strong in one is not automatically useful in another, and parents routinely describe the wrong one on a first call.

PYP sets no external papers, so tuition at that stage is about reading fluency, number sense and the habit of explaining an answer rather than only producing one. MYP is where families in Sion usually first ask for help, because MYP reporting is criterion-based: each subject group is marked against criteria A to D on eight-point scales, and a child can write a page of correct content and still score a four because the task asked for analysis and received description. MYP 5 adds the Personal Project, assessed on its own criteria, which quietly eats weekends from September onwards.

IGCSE brings the first decision that follows a child for two years: Core or Extended. Core caps the grade available; Extended opens the full range and adds both content and a harder paper. Schools stream for this in Year 9 or early Year 10, often before a parent has understood the consequence. An IGCSE tutor's first job is frequently not content at all, it is working out whether the child is in the right tier and whether a move is still possible this year.

The Diploma Programme is a different animal: six subjects at Higher Level (HL) or Standard Level (SL), plus Theory of Knowledge (TOK), the Extended Essay (EE) and Creativity, Activity, Service. Every subject carries an Internal Assessment (IA) marked at school and moderated by the IB, so the marks that decide a Diploma are spread across two years. A DP1 who treats the first year as a warm-up spends DP2 repairing it. An IB and IGCSE tutor Mumbai families keep for two years is usually the one who fits the schedule, not the one with the longest subject list.
bullets: PYP: no external exams, so tuition targets reading, number sense and explanation.
